title: How to Fix Dents After BBL?
meta_description: Swelling can hide your results for months. How often contour irregularities happen, what the FDA says about filler, and when to ask about a revision.
excerpt: Swelling can hide your results, and it sometimes takes 3 to 6 months to subside. Here is how often contour irregularities are reported, what the FDA says about filler, what no source can tell you, and when to have a surgeon look.
quick_answer:
How do you fix dents after a BBL?

Start with an exam, because The Aesthetic Society says swelling sometimes takes 3 to 6 months to subside. A 2026 meta-analysis found contour irregularities in 2.29% of cases. An ASPS article says some patients return for another BBL to smooth them. The FDA recommends against filler for body contouring, including the buttocks.

notes: Quotes came through WebFetch, whose extraction model caps a quote at about 125 characters, so long sentences are split or end early; the two ASPS PDFs were read with pdftotext instead (the report PDF exceeded WebFetch's size limit, so it was fetched with plain curl). Title and H2 wording kept, opening H2 added with a short answer, FDA filler wording kept from the Batch 0 edit. Changed: "10-20%" (now Elsaftawy 2.29%, labelled as not a dent rate); massage redistributing fat and "excellent results"; "viable solutions"; the caffeine and retinol benefit claims; 6-month, 6-12 month, 4-6 week and 2-4 week figures; the 6-week garment line, because garment weeks can't be stated as the practice's protocol; plural and board-certified surgeons; "countless patients"; "best" (sweep); "poor surgical technique" (disparaging, and "common" is unsourced); phone numbers and #contactus.
